newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fischler pledges penalties for cruelty in transit.
newsitem.headline: Fischler pledges penalties for cruelty in transit.

text.p: The European Commission is to propose the withdrawal of export aid to animal exporters who do not respect European rules on the welfare of live animals in transport, EU farm commissioner Franz Fischler said on Tuesday.
Fischler said he expected the Commission to submit a proposal to the European Union Council of Ministers and the European Parliament by the end of April.
The commissioner was responding to concerns from Euro-MPs that cattle exported to third countries for slaughter were being subject to appalling conditions.
Finnish Euro-MP Astrid Thors said figures showed the EU had forked out 296 million Ecus in subsidies for live cattle exports between October 1995 and October 1996.
She said the best way to stop the cruelty was to end the subsidies.

The commissioner said checks were carried out on transport lorries and ships in the EU but the Commission was having problems trying to monitor the state of animals arriving at their final destinations.
He said the Commission was liaising with animal welfare groups to carry out these controls.
